value.title: /pij ready on the Rust system — generation-aware CLI + lifecycle verb parity
value.complexity_breakdown: CS-3: the routing shim is small and well-bounded; the verb port is many small surfaces against an existing daemon, parallelisable by verb.
value.confidence: high — the target surface is a shipped TS CLI whose behaviour is observable, and the acceptance is one operator gesture
value.summary: Jordan types /pij ready and lands in the NEW system. PRD req-0010 + req-0011.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: `/pij ready` is not stale — it runs `pij adopt` / `pij whoami` / `pij report`, and `pij` on PATH is the TypeScript CLI, so a seat reporting ready registers into the LEGACY store and is invisible to the rs daemon (observed live 2026-09-01: pij-fierce-xoxarle absent from `pij-rs list`). Two halves fix it. ROUTE (req-0011): one `pij` command that detects a live rs daemon and sends verbs there, falling back to legacy per-verb when rs lacks one — so nothing downstream learns a second binary name. PARITY (req-0010): implement the missing lifecycle verbs in rs, in the order real usage ranks them (PR #329's telemetry, not taste). Routing lands first so parity arrives invisibly, verb by verb.

sections.name: goals
value: Typing `/pij ready` in a fresh seat registers it into the RS store, with no skill edit and no human typing `pij-rs`.
`pij whoami` names that seat from rs; `pij report now` writes its card to rs; `pij state <id>` reads it back.
A verb rs does not implement falls back to LEGACY and still works — migration is invisible, never a cliff.
The operator can always find out which generation served a verb, and can force either one.

sections.name: non_goals
value: No orchestration verbs (batons, projects, fences, streams) — telemetry shows they barely register; they wait.
No consent-default change: crossSessionInbound stays opt-in (coupled to plan 110's held backoff).
No data migration between the legacy store and the rs store — a seat lives in whichever registered it. If a seat must move, that is its own row.
No rewrite of the /pij skill or any packet — if a doc must change for this to work, the routing design is wrong.

value.claim: THE OPERATOR GESTURE, closing in TWO STAGES (ac-1141 is not closable from a worktree — `which pij` resolves to the shared canonical checkout). STAGE A (this PR): unmodified /pij ready in a fresh seat, under a per-seat pij-entry/PATH override, lands the seat in `pij-rs list` with pane and proc — receipt says EXACTLY 'skill unmodified, pij RESOLUTION overridden', never 'unmodified environment'. STAGE B (post-merge deploy, o-prime owned, recorded on req-0011): canonical pulls, Jordan performs the real gesture with no override. WAVE NOTE: the end-to-end arm is declared RED UNTIL WAVE 2 and must be stated as such, not quietly deferred — rs has no adopt route in wave 1 and forcing it green would require minting in the shim, which ac-1147 forbids.
`pij whoami` names that seat and reports it was served by rs; `pij report now "x" "y"` writes a card readable via the rs daemon; `pij state <id>` returns it.

Fallback is per-verb and inspectable with THREE DISTINGUISHABLE outcomes (never collapsed — F-1128): routed-to-rs / rs-does-not-implement-so-legacy / seat-lives-in-legacy-so-legacy-FOLLOWED. An rs ERROR never falls back. Forceback works both directions, and the diagnostic names both the generation AND THE ADDR that served (two rs daemons have already coexisted on this machine). WIRING IS PART OF THIS CRITERION, NOT AN EXTRA: each named outcome must be REACHABLE FROM THE PRODUCTION CALL SITE, not merely present and unit-tested. Wave 1 shipped `legacy-seat-followed` unreachable — defaultRouterDeps() supplied none of ambientSeatId/seatInLegacy/seatInRs — so oq-1141's ruling had no production existence. The receipt must answer one question per outcome: does the production call site supply what this guard needs?
rs `report` covers now/state/blocked/clear/verify/question with the SAME argument shapes callers already type; a shape rs cannot honour refuses by name rather than silently differing.

THE FALSE FRIEND STAYS DENIED, whatever computes the routed set. `tail` is on an explicit deny list that the dispatcher CONSULTS (a decorative NEVER_ROUTED list that nothing reads was found and fixed in wave 1). Pinned by a test that puts `tail` INTO the routed set and asserts denial anyway, including under force:rs. REASON CORRECTED 2026-09-01: the original wording justified this by 'a capability-derived router removes the deliberate act' — the delivered router is a deny scan plus a table, so that reason is false on tree. The true and always-sufficient reason: future plans add rows, and a false friend must FAIL A TEST before it can ever be routed.

No downstream artifact changed — TWO ARMS PROVING TWO DIFFERENT CLAIMS (they are one artifact on two checkouts, NOT two independent proofs; the installed skill resolves to this repo's own tracked skills/pij). ARM A: repo diff touches zero files under skills/ or .claude/ — proves no coder on this branch edited the skill; this arm is hermetic and is why the AC exists. ARM B: installed-tree hash WITH canonical's HEAD sha recorded beside it — a foreign-mutation detector proving nothing else changed the installed surface during the witness, and attributable (another fleet swapping canonical) rather than merely detectable.

ONE MINTER: rs adopt MINTS the seat id (memorable-id allocator, already oracle-tested in rs); the shim never invents a name and rs `register` keeps caller-supplied ids for the explicit case only. Pinned by a test that the shim has no name-generation path.

`phonehome` is served by rs for an rs-registered seat — never by legacy (it is inside the ready gesture itself, and legacy answering for an rs seat is the identity violation this plan exists to prevent). rs adopt binds synchronously where it can, so phonehome confirms rather than polls.

sections.name: risks_assumptions
sections.value: RISK 1 — SPLIT-BRAIN IDENTITY is the headline risk: the same seat registered in both stores, or a seat that adopts into rs while its peers still resolve it in legacy, yields messages that vanish with every surface reporting success. Mitigation: routing is per-VERB but identity is per-SEAT — once a seat registers into a generation, every identity verb for that seat must resolve to the SAME generation, and the fallback must never silently re-home a seat. Name the rule explicitly and test it. RISK 2 — a fallback that hides a real rs failure: rs erroring must NOT fall back to legacy (that would mask defects and re-home seats); only rs NOT IMPLEMENTING a verb falls back. The two cases must be distinguishable at the call site — same lesson as F-1128 (a notice that cannot tell its cases apart carries no information). RISK 3 — the false friend (`tail`) silently serving the wrong object; retired by ac-1145. ASSUMPTION — the rs daemon's HTTP surface can carry the report/whoami/adopt semantics without schema migration; if a verb needs a store column, that is in fence and gets a migration test. RISK 6 (PM O3, ruled at the ack): two id MINTERS would create two namespaces and the headline split-brain by construction — u-identity is not a port, it is a decision about where the minter lives. RULED: the minter lives in rs. RISK 7 (PM O1): the shim governs nothing the operator types until it lands in the shared canonical checkout, so a worktree witness is necessarily partial — hence ac-1141's two stages; branch-swapping canonical is FORBIDDEN (fleet-wide blast radius). RISK 8 (ruled at wave 1): a capability-ASK router cannot drift from what rs serves — strictly better than a hardcoded table — but it REMOVES the deliberate act that kept `tail` unrouted, so it must be intersected with an explicit deny list. RISK 9: an UNANSWERABLE capability ask is an ERROR, never 'does not implement' — otherwise an rs that cannot answer silently re-homes every verb to legacy. Corollary already found on tree: `require_bearer` layers the whole router and rejects 401 before route match, so a wrong key reads as route-absence — a credential fault wearing a capability fault's clothes; 401 is a named, tested, no-fallback outcome. RISK 10 (wave 1, self-caught by the PM): a guard declared, tested and UNREACHABLE reads as coverage — the third form of computed-but-unconsulted. It was hidden by being accidentally right (no rs handler exists, so every routed verb fell to legacy regardless) and becomes FLEET-BREAKING the day /v1/report matches: most seats on this box are legacy-resident, and under the never-bare-404 rule the only legal answer becomes an envelope refusal, i.e. rs-error, i.e. exit 4 — `pij report now` breaks fleet-wide. Retired by ac-1143's wiring clause.

value.question: When BOTH daemons are live and a seat exists only in legacy, should an identity verb for that seat route to legacy automatically (follow the seat) or refuse and tell the operator to migrate?
value.note: Recommendation to rule at the ack: FOLLOW THE SEAT, because a refusal breaks a fleet mid-flight; but it must be VISIBLE in the diagnostic, never silent.
